title: Wolf and Veil
premise: Bram Hartwell, a cartographer who has never left the magic-dead valley of her birth, inherits a living map from a dying stranger — a map that drags her bodily into the realm it depicts. There she falls in with a ragged company guarding the last dragon, whose fading fire holds an ancient war in check; among them is Kaelen, a wolf-bonded sentinel sworn to kill anyone who carries what Bram now carries: the stranger's secret bloodline, heir to both warring thrones. As dragon-fire gutters and duty demands her death, Bram must choose between the inheritance that could reignite the war and the found family that claims her heart. In the end she burns the claim itself, feeding the last dragon's flame with her inherited right to rule, and chooses a home drawn by her own hand rather than one drawn for her.
about_author: Orsen Sterling is the pen name of a former trail-surveyor who spent a decade mapping remote highlands before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people who inherit burdens they never asked for, usually accompanied by at least one large animal.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She finishes a commission map of the valley no one leaves, establishing her restlessness and the rule that magic cannot cross its borders. A storm brings a wounded stranger to her door. Emotional beat: quiet longing cracked open by intrusion.

chapters.title: Ink and Blood
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The dying stranger presses a folded map into Bram's hands and dies whispering about 'the last fire.' The map moves under her fingers like a living thing. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Pulled Through
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Attempting to burn the map, she is instead dragged through it into the realm of Veyra — a forest where trees remember names. She is found by Kaelen, a wolf-bonded sentinel, who nearly kills her on sight. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Company of the Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. He reports the stranger to his found-family company: hedge-witch Sable, exiled knight Dorn, and child thief Pip. They shelter Bram because killing map-carriers is forbidden by their old oath. Emotional beat: wary hospitality masking suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Map Wants
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The map redraws itself nightly, showing a path toward the Emberhold, lair of the last dragon. Kaelen teaches her the roads; friction becomes grudging respect. Emotional beat: first warmth between strangers bound by duty.

chapters.title: Wolves Do Not Lie
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. His wolf, Ash, refuses to scent Bram as human — hinting at her hidden bloodline. Kaelen conceals this from the company, torn between oath and instinct. Emotional beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Duskmere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The company crosses contested territory; toll-keepers demand a memory as payment, and Bram pays one of her valley childhood. Pip comforts her. Emotional beat: grief for what the journey already costs.

chapters.title: Ashes of the First War
chapters.summary: Dorn's POV. Passing a battlefield frozen mid-slaughter by old dragon-fire, he recounts how the war ended: two royal lines annihilated, peace sealed only by the dragon's burning breath. Emotional beat: history pressing its weight onto the present.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margins
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Studying the map's marginalia, she finds her own family name written as royalty — the stranger was her aunt, and Bram is the lost heir of both warring houses. Emotional beat: identity shattering.

chapters.title: The Sentinel's Oath
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. He confesses to Sable that the heir lives; oath-bound, someone must kill Bram before rival factions learn of her. Sable argues the oath can be reinterpreted. Emotional beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: Emberhold Rising
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The company reaches the volcano-fortress and meets Vess, the last dragon — ancient, dying, and sardonic. Vess smells Bram's blood immediately and says nothing. Emotional beat: awe laced with foreboding.

chapters.title: Fire Lessons
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vess teaches her that dragon-fire is fed by legitimate claim; the flame gutters because no true heir tends it. Bram begins secretly feeding it, feeling the war's peace steady. Emotional beat: purpose discovered, burden accepted.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. Rival faction scouts track the company; a skirmish forces them to flee the Emberhold's approaches. Kaelen saves Bram's life and realizes he cannot be her executioner. Emotional beat: duty cracking under love.

chapters.title: Confession at the Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. He tells Bram the truth: her blood makes her a target, and his oath once made him her intended killer. Bram's fury and hurt nearly break the company apart. Emotional beat: betrayal, then fragile honesty.

chapters.title: Pip's Bargain
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The child thief steals the map to sell it and save the starving company, then returns it, having read enough to understand what Bram carries. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other over survival.

chapters.title: The Siege of Emberhold
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Both remnant armies converge on the fortress, each wanting the heir as a weapon. The company defends the gates while dragon-fire dims dangerously. Emotional beat: rising dread as every choice narrows.

chapters.title: Two Thrones, One Heart
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Captured briefly by the faction leaders, Bram is offered everything — crowns, restoration, revenge — if she claims her birthright and leads them. She sees herself becoming the war. Emotional beat: temptation met with clarity.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. Dragon-fire fails; the ancient truce collapses and battle erupts inside the caldera. Kaelen fights to reach Bram through the melee, Ash falling protecting Pip. Emotional beat: climax of loss and desperation.

chapters.title: What Bram Burns
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the dragon's side, Bram feeds her claim — the entire inherited right to both thrones — into the last fire, erasing herself as heir forever. The flame roars back to life and freezes both armies mid-stride. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-definition.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Chosen Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The armies scatter, leaderless but alive; the company mourns Ash and reckons with what Bram gave up. Vess, restored, offers her anything in return. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: A Map Drawn by Hand
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram draws a new map — not inherited but authored — charting a valley like home where the company might live, magic and all. Kaelen asks, not as sentinel but as man, to be shown the way. Emotional beat: love chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: Wolf and Veil
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, closing. One year later: the company settled, Vess circling overhead, the old map framed and blank. Bram adds a final border to her new map and signs it. Emotional beat: peace earned, inheritance transformed into legacy.
